site.name: climate-almanac
site.summary: Climate Almanac — multi-variable climate explorer (local demo) Fictional climate-data explorer. Local fixture for UXBench. Open `index.html` directly. Page `index.html` — Explorer Three-panel layout: left rail variable selector (six climate variables, each with a colored swatch, units, and source caption), center chart area, right inspector panel. Center stack: - A vector chart with up to four overlaid series and a dual-axis option (left axis for unit-less anomalies, right for absolute units). - Hovering exposes a value tooltip and updates the right-rail inspector with the same year's values.

explored_user_goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full climate-almanac system, prioritizing the primary data visualization flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_summary: The climate-almanac explorer effectively visualizes multi-variable data and adapts its layout well across viewports. However, it suffers from significant state synchronization bugs, most notably failing to update chart titles or clear the chart when all variables are unselected. Furthermore, missing interaction feedback on core actions (sharing, exporting, adding notes) and undersized mobile tap targets degrade confidence and usability.

exploration_plan.goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full climate-almanac system, prioritizing the primary data visualization flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_plan.summary: The exploration will focus on the single-page application `index.html`, starting with core variable selection and layer management to test the 4-variable limit. Next, it will evaluate the data modifiers (Region, Smoothing, Y-Axis) and their effect on the chart. Following that, chart tools (Add Note, Reset Zoom) and top-level actions (Share, Download) will be tested. Finally, the run will validate the mobile experience, paying special attention to layout collapse and reported small tap targets.
assumptions: The application is a single-page app built in index.html, so navigation links (Datasets, Stories, etc.) likely point to '#' or act as placeholders.
Hover interactions might be difficult to fully validate via the agent, so we will focus on clickable elements like adding notes and deleting annotations.
Chart rendering relies on canvas/SVG which we evaluate visually; state changes should reflect in title/label updates or visual shifts.
risk_hotspots: Handling of the 'up to four variables' limit (error message vs disabled checkboxes)
Usability of the 'LAYERS DRAG TO REORDER' section and layer deletion ('×' buttons)
Mobile layout collapsing for the three-panel design
Small tap targets across top navigation and left-rail checkboxes on mobile devices

phases.title: Variables & Layers Management
phases.objective: Validate variable selection, the maximum of 4 variables constraint, and layer removal.
key_checks: Select additional variables to hit the 4-variable limit and observe system feedback
Deselect a variable via the left-rail checkbox
Remove a selected variable using the '×' button in the LAYERS section
exit_criteria: Variables can be added/removed, and the 4-variable limit is triggered and handled gracefully.

phases.title: Data Modifiers
phases.objective: Test the global controls for Region, Smoothing, and Y-Axis.
key_checks: Change the 'REGION' dropdown and check for UI updates
exit_criteria: All select and radio button modifier controls can be interacted with without errors.

phases.title: Chart Tools & Annotations
phases.objective: Interact with chart specific functionalities like zoom, notes, and the inspector panel.
key_checks: Click '+ Note' to see how new annotations are created
Click the '×' on an existing annotation in the right panel to delete it
exit_criteria: Note addition flow is exposed, zoom resets, and annotations can be deleted.

phases.title: Top-level Actions & Export
phases.objective: Test the utility buttons and header navigation.
key_checks: Click 'Share view' and observe outcome (e.g., clipboard copy, modal)
Click one of the secondary nav links (e.g., 'Datasets') to verify behavior
exit_criteria: Export and share actions are triggered; nav links are verified as placeholders or functional.

phases.title: Mobile Viewport Validation
phases.objective: Evaluate the responsive layout and accessibility of small tap targets on mobile.
key_checks: Verify that the left rail, center chart, and right inspector stack correctly without horizontal scrolling
Attempt to tap checkboxes and header links to validate the small tap target warnings
exit_criteria: Mobile layout is reviewed and tap target usability is assessed.

coverage_targets.features: Select variables, change modifiers, use chart tools, delete annotations, test exports.
coverage_targets.mobile: Ensure the 3-column layout adapts to a mobile screen and controls remain usable.

notes: Since it's a data visualization, pay close attention to the chart title updates (e.g., 'Surface temperature anomaly & Atmospheric CO2') when changing variables or modifiers, as this is a good proxy for successful state changes.

findings.user_goal: Understand which data and parameters are currently being visualized.
findings.problem: The main chart title and subtitle do not dynamically update to reflect the user's active selections.
findings.evidence: When checking/unchecking variables (e.g., adding Precipitation or removing Atmospheric CO2), the title remains 'Surface temperature anomaly & Atmospheric CO₂'. Similarly, changing Region to 'Northern Hemisphere' or Smoothing to 'No smoothing' fails to update the 'Global' and '3-year running mean' subtitle.
findings.why_it_matters: Stale metadata creates a severe mismatch between the visual plot and the text description, leading to misinterpretation of the data and loss of trust.
findings.suggestion: Bind the chart title and subtitle dynamically to the active variable selections, region state, and smoothing state.
findings.source_hint: Chart title and subtitle text nodes

findings.user_goal: Clear the visualization to start over or view an empty state.
findings.problem: The chart fails to update to an empty state when all variable checkboxes are deselected.
findings.evidence: When all variables are unchecked in the left panel, the previously selected data series remains visible on the chart rather than disappearing.
findings.why_it_matters: Users expect the visual output to perfectly mirror the input controls. If deselecting everything leaves data behind, the application state appears broken.
findings.suggestion: Implement an empty state for the chart that clears the SVG/Canvas when the active layers array length is 0, optionally showing a prompt like 'Select a variable to begin'.

findings.user_goal: Export the data or share the current view.
findings.problem: Global actions like 'Share view' and 'Download .csv' provide no immediate visual feedback.
findings.evidence: Clicking 'Share view' or 'Download .csv' yields no toast notification, loading spinner, or success message.
findings.why_it_matters: Without feedback, users are left guessing whether the application registered their click, potentially leading to repeated clicks or frustration if the download takes time to start.
findings.suggestion: Add brief visual feedback, such as a toast saying 'Link copied to clipboard' or a temporary loading state on the download button.

findings.user_goal: Add a contextual note or annotation to a specific year.
findings.problem: The '+ Note' button provides no clear instruction or immediate flow for creating an annotation.
findings.evidence: Clicking '+ Note' does not bring up an input field, modal, or instructional prompt, leaving it entirely unclear how the user should proceed (e.g., if they need to select a year first).
findings.why_it_matters: Features with invisible or hidden prerequisites block users from utilizing them entirely.
findings.suggestion: When '+ Note' is clicked, either open a modal to select a year and type a note, or display a clear inline prompt like 'Click a year on the chart to add a note.'

findings.user_goal: Identify the data series plotted on the chart via the legend.
findings.problem: Legend text overlaps and becomes unreadable when multiple variables are activated.
findings.evidence: When 3 or 4 variables are selected (e.g., adding ENSO index and Global mean sea level), the legend item text at the top of the chart overlaps heavily.
findings.why_it_matters: An illegible legend prevents users from matching chart lines to their corresponding variable and units.
findings.suggestion: Implement text wrapping, dynamic spacing, or a flexbox layout for the chart legend to ensure labels never overlap, regardless of how many are active.

findings.user_goal: Toggle variables and adjust axes comfortably on a mobile device.
findings.problem: Core form controls have extremely small touch targets on mobile viewports.
findings.evidence: The variable checkboxes and Y-axis radio buttons have tap targets of 13x13px, and the layer/annotation 'x' delete buttons are 20x18px, well below the standard 44px mobile guidance.
findings.why_it_matters: Small tap targets cause "fat-finger" errors, frustrating mobile users who may accidentally toggle the wrong variable or fail to tap the control entirely.
findings.suggestion: Increase the padding and minimum height/width of checkboxes, radios, and delete buttons to ensure they have at least a 44x44px functional touch area.
findings.source_hint: ux-3 to ux-8, ux-11, ux-12, ux-66

findings.user_goal: Understand and adhere to the system's limitations for data overlays.
findings.problem: The stated limit of four variables is not enforced by the system.
findings.evidence: The UI states 'Add up to four variables to overlay', but a user was able to successfully check and add a 5th variable (Arctic sea-ice extent) to the chart without any error or restriction.
findings.why_it_matters: Inconsistent rules break mental models. If the system can handle 5 variables, the text is unnecessarily restrictive; if it can't, the lack of enforcement will lead to broken UI (like the overlapping legend).
findings.suggestion: Either update the copy to reflect the true technical limit, or disable remaining checkboxes once four variables are actively selected.

findings.user_goal: Understand and interact with dropdown menus using assistive technology.
findings.problem: Dropdown select elements are missing accessible labels.
findings.evidence: Layout warnings indicate that the select elements for 'REGION' (ux-9) and 'SMOOTHING' (ux-10) lack a `<label>`, `aria-label`, or `placeholder`.
findings.why_it_matters: Screen reader users will not be able to determine what these dropdowns control when navigating to them, severely impairing accessibility.
findings.suggestion: Add explicit `<label>` elements linked via `id` to the select inputs, or provide descriptive `aria-label` attributes.
